CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain after injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a left ankle injury yesterday while on a walk with his wife. He stepped off a curb and landed on his ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing or feeling a pop but reports the ankle felt extended and stretched. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle. He was able to walk back to his house after the incident, though it was painful. Pain has been present for a couple of days. He rates his pain as 8/10 without medication and 7/10 with ibuprofen or acetaminophen. He has been managing the injury with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight avoidance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Patient denies any substantial previous injuries to the left ankle.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (used for current ankle pain).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He and his wife take walks regularly.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals stable with slight elevation attributed to pain. Focused exam of left ankle reveals ecchymosis and swelling over the lateral malleolus with edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with soft tissue swelling. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot. Neurovascular exam: capillary refill brisk (less than 3 seconds), strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, motor and sensation intact bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: no fracture or bony abnormalities.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, compression, elevation). Prescribed air cast for ankle stabilization and crutches to remain off the leg but allow walking as tolerated. Continue NSAIDs to reduce pain and swelling. Symptoms expected to improve significantly over 4-7 days. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if pain worsens or if he has any concerns.
